messages:
Olivia S.: FYI ticket #SUP-4821 — ACME Global says their payment failed and the invoice they received is in EUR but their local entities asked for GBP/PLN invoices + PO on file. Invoice: 2024-ACME-789. Customer says card declined and the charge amount doesn't match invoice by a few cents. Blocking onboarding. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/SUP-4821
Emma C.: ack — can you paste the payment attempt details? gateway decline code, charge id, and whether invoice was auto-generated or manual? cc @Raj P.
BillingBot: Payment attempt logged: attempt_id=pay_0a9f3e, status=failed, error=card_declined, gateway_code=402_PAY_MISMATCH, currency_attempt=GBP, currency_invoice=EUR, amount_invoice=124.57, amount_attempt=124.56
Raj P.: pulling ledger... I see invoice was created in EUR under entity_id=ent-acme-eu, but the customer account mapping caused the charge to be attempted in GBP (entity->billing currency mapping). FX conversion used rate 0.8793 rounded to 2 decimals -> small rounding diff ~0.01. Need to check gateway tolerance for amount mismatch. Can we repro in staging?
Marco L.: can you paste the API payload or the admin actions that created the invoice? if we can replay we'll see where rounding applied.
Olivia S.: copying the minimal debug payload used by support (redacted):
```
POST /v1/invoices
{
  "customer_id": "acct-acme-global",
  "entity_id": "ent-acme-eu",
  "line_items": [{"desc":"Platform usage","qty":1,"unit_amount":124.57}],
  "currency": "EUR",
  "po_number": "PO-99321",
  "tax_id": "",
  "auto_charge": true
}

POST /v1/payments
{
  "invoice_id": "2024-ACME-789",
  "method": "card",
  "currency": "GBP",
  "card_last4": "4242"
}
```
Emma C.: thanks. so the invoice in EUR but payments service forced GBP capture because the customer entity mapping defaulted to GBP. support clicked "charge" in UI which used customer settings.
Raj P.: repro steps I recommend for staging: 1) create customer with multi-entity mapping (entity A: EUR, entity B: GBP). 2) create invoice in EUR but set auto_charge and customer.default_currency=GBP. 3) run charge flow and capture gateway request payload. check the exchange_rate logic in billing-service and the rounding mode (banker's vs half-up).
Marco L.: good call. I reproduced in staging — our conversion uses Math.round(amount * 100) after applying rate, which loses fractions under 0.5c. Gateway expects amount to match invoice cents when converted with high precision; a 0.01 mismatch triggers 402_PAY_MISMATCH in our test gateway.
Lina T.: tax note — for intra-EU multi-entity invoices we usually need VAT numbers and correct reverse-charge flags. If customer wants local currency invoices per legal entity, we should issue separate invoices per entity, not a consolidated cross-entity invoice. That avoids currency inversion during charge.
Emma C.: I re-ran a test: created two invoices per entity in correct local currency and triggered charges — both succeeded. Then I created the single-consolidated invoice but forced capture_amount = precise_unrounded_amount -> gateway accepted it. So short-term fixes: reissue per-entity local invoices OR send corrected capture amount to gateway.
Olivia S.: Customer-facing suggested steps: 1) reissue the invoice(s) in the requested local currencies per legal entity and include PO numbers (they require PO per-entity). 2) resend payment link or accept bank transfer. 3) apologize and offer to waive any rounding adjustment. Want me to proceed?
Raj P.: I'll reissue invoices for ACME: ent-acme-uk (GBP) and ent-acme-pl (PLN) and include the PO numbers. Also opening ticket with gateway ops to relax strict mismatch threshold or accept 2-decimal rounding tolerance. I can action this within 2 business hours.
Marco L.: I'll open a PR to change conversion rounding to use BigDecimal with half-up rounding to 4 decimals before cent conversion and add a unit test reproducing our staging case. Also will add an opt-in switch that allows forcing "precise_capture" when invoice currency != charge currency.
Lina T.: finance/tax will confirm if reissuing per-entity is okay for accounting; for EU entities we need VAT on the invoice otherwise they'll refuse. Please attach VAT numbers.
Emma C.: customer was OK with us reissuing per-entity. I created a staging invoice_preview that matched their expectations.
Olivia S.: Action list for SUPPORT -> FINANCE: reissue two invoices, send new pay links, mark SUP-4821 as escalated to Billing. Raj please update when done.
Raj P.: done — invoices reissued (2024-ACME-789-UK, 2024-ACME-789-PL). Payment link sent. Customer responded they paid via bank transfer (confirmed by bank_rails at 2024-03-19T10:04Z). Escalated gateway tolerance to ops ticket GATE-1284.
Olivia S.: awesome. closing loop with customer and letting them know we'll follow up about gateway config and internal rounding fix. :thumbsup:
Emma C.: noted — moving to resolved. I'll attach the repro steps and the staging logs to SUP-4821 for future reference.
BillingBot: SUP-4821 status updated -> resolved (paid by bank transfer).
